taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and native to Texas at state scale.
look_here_first: Inspect several mature LEAF SHEATHS closely: bigtop often has conspicuous hairs on the sheath, especially along the upper margins and near the apex, sometimes extending across much of its surface. The existing close-up shows abundant long hairs beyond just the collar. But sheath pubescence varies, and a single hairy collar does not prove E. hirsuta. Compare the large open panicle, lower branch axils and mature spikelets with plains and sand lovegrass; keep uncertain plants at Eragrostis sp.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Uvalde is the only exact project target-zone county currently locked. Statewide Texas nativity and the old Hays-local flag are not county proof.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification.

best_field_traits: ciliate sheath mouth and hairy ligule
morphology_keys.comparison_training: E. intermedia is much more glabrous on the sheaths; E. trichodes concentrates hairs near the sheath apex rather than across the sheath surface.
crew_field_walkthrough: Step 1 — Whole rooted perennial clump: photograph size, foliage distribution, and full open mature panicle.
Step 2 — Lower and middle sheaths: photograph the HAIRS ON THE SHEATH SURFACE (not merely the throat). Compare multiple culms.
Step 3 — Open one mature leaf collar: photograph sheath mouth, short hair-fringe ligule and any ciliate margins with a hand lens.
Step 4 — Inspect the branching head: photograph bearded lower panicle branch axils, separately from the leaf nodes and collars.
Step 5 — Take an intact spikelet beside millimeter divisions; if only overall panicle size is visible, leave the plant at Eragrostis sp.
morphology_keys.what_to_teach_crew: Hairy across the sheath = think BIGTOP. Hair only at the opening does not prove bigtop. Use a sheath closeup, the open inflorescence and axils together; compare plains and sand lovegrass rather than guessing by color.
overlap_cautions: Collar hairs alone occur in E. intermedia and E. trichodes; the distribution of hairs over the sheath surface is more informative.
A fuzzy-looking inflorescence is not proof of E. hirsuta; panicle branch axils must actually be inspected.
Native statewide does not establish nativity in Hays County; current target-zone native-range verdict remains unresolved.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with E. intermedia and E. trichodes, examine several complete leaf sheaths: E. hirsuta has conspicuous hairs ON THE SHEATH SURFACE, not only concentrated at the sheath throat. Pair this with lower panicle axil beard and broad open panicle; E. spectabilis has a striking wide, often purple inflorescence but is not identified by color.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Bigtop lovegrass: sheath first, panicle second
steps: Choose multiple mature leaf sheaths; compare hairs on the surface, upper sheath margins and collar, not a single tuft.
Find the open panicle and photograph several branch junctions in focus; existing panicle photos are good for shape but do not prove axil-beard identity.
Add a side-on ligule image and two mature spikelets beside millimeter scale. If the details are absent, stay at Eragrostis sp.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: If all you have is an airy panicle, label it Eragrostis sp. until a sheath is photographed.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The observed sheath hair photos are anatomy references, not a voucher-level independently confirmed species determination.

visual_comparison.title: Bigtop lovegrass — diagnose the HAIRY SHEATH
visual_comparison.subtitle: Existing CC0 sheath image shows the strongest comparison character. Four screen arrows across three real image panels; fine reproductive anatomy still needs matched macros.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: BIGTOP = noticeably hairy SHEATH BODY. Hairy COLLAR alone? Not sufficient.

items.label: 1 — Real sheath hairs, not just a hairy-looking seedhead

items.caption: The CC0 source photograph clearly shows long hairs growing from green leaf sheaths at multiple levels, plus tufts near the blade/sheath junction. Both arrows target these visible hairs; this image does not measure the ligule or independently verify the complete taxon.
items.why_it_matters: The distribution of hairs ON the sheath is the fastest high-value visual distinction from plains and sand lovegrass.
